messages:
rebecca_support: FYI customer (acct redwood-acme) seeing intermittent 429s in last 20m during a traffic spike. They've pasted sample response headers and req-ids below. Can someone confirm if this is quota enforcement or a bug? :thinking:

rebecca_support: Samples:
- req id: req_01a2b3c4  status: 429  headers: x-rate-limit-limit:100, x-rate-limit-remaining:0, x-rate-limit-reset: 1769123460
- req id: req_01a2b3c5  status: 200  headers: x-rate-limit-remaining:5
- req id: req_01a2b3c6  status: 429  headers: x-rate-limit-remaining:0

rebecca_support: Short timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-17T15:02:10Z first burst observed
- 2026-03-17T15:03:05Z 429s begin (multiple req ids)
- 2026-03-17T15:05:40Z burst subsides (~120s total)

sam_oncall: tagging @aria for quota rules. Initial look: headers indicate rate limiting. Can you attach HAR or a curl loop so we can reproduce locally?

rebecca_support: uploaded debug bundle and HAR: s3://redwood-support/debugs/1769123456/redwood-acme-har.zip. Customer also shared the curl loop they used: 
```
for i in {1..60}; do curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 0.2; done
```
They mention their SDK does retries which may have platooned requests.

aria_eng: I ran a quick repro on staging with the same per-key policy. When sustained requests exceed ~20 rps for >30s we hit the token-bucket floor and we emit 429s. We're seeing two enforcement layers: per-route QPS and a global per-key burst bucket. Sample log for req_01a2b3c4:
```
2026-03-17T15:03:05.123Z INF rate_limiter allow=false key=sk-acme-xxx route=/v1/generate burst_tokens=0 window_remaining_ms=1800
```

aria_eng: Controlled repro command I ran on staging: 
```
seq 1 40 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code} %{url_effective}\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx\" https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Result: ~35% 429s during mid-window. My observed request ids: req_stg_9f3b, req_stg_a12c.

sam_oncall: OK. Please confirm whether the customer is sharing one API key across many short-lived workers (that pattern often causes bursts). Also request exact request ids + timestamps for all 429s to map to infra logs.

rebecca_support: Customer reply: running sdk-js v0.39 with default backoff, fronted by many ephemeral lambda workers all using the same key. They gave exact 429 headers and timestamps (UTC):
- 2026-03-17T15:03:05Z req: req_01a2b3c4 headers: x-rate-limit-limit:100,x-rate-limit-remaining:0,x-rate-limit-reset:1769123460
- 2026-03-17T15:04:22Z req: req_01a2b3c6 headers: x-rate-limit-remaining:0,x-rate-limit-reset:1769123522

rate-limit-bot: Automated note: key=sk-acme-xxx exceeded per-key burst threshold at 2026-03-17T15:03:05Z; next reset window 2026-03-17T15:04:20Z

aria_eng: Triage summary: behavior matches quota enforcement given high concurrency on a shared key. Mitigation options:
- rotate keys per worker (one key per instance)
- add jitter + exponential backoff in client retries
- request a Dedicated quota bump or higher burst allowance for this customer (sales/CS).

rebecca_support: I'll send the recommended steps to the customer and open a quota increase request. Also asked them to provide a minimal curl reproduction of the failure (with their key redacted) and any HARs for exact mapping. Thanks! :thumbsup:

sam_oncall: Marking this investigation as resolved unless the customer demonstrates different behavior or we find internal miscount. Closing for now.
